::: {.bnr-manual-flag .bnr-manual-flag--operations}
Operations Manual
:::

The private REDCap Data Access Register is the authoritative record for applications, decisions, agreements, releases and closure. Do not manage a request through email alone or create a separate local register.

## 1. Receive and classify

The applicant completes the public **Data Access Application** survey. Confirm that the record identifies the applicant, organisation, purpose, population, period, minimum variables, planned outputs, ethics position and security arrangements.

First check whether an existing approved public output meets the need. If not, classify the minimum information required as a new aggregate output, restricted de-identified record-level data, or identifiable/linkable data requiring referral.

Do not describe record-level data as anonymous merely because direct identifiers have been removed.

## 2. Review and decide

Complete the **BNR Review and Decision** instrument. Record the review of:

- purpose and public-health value;
- minimum necessary data;
- ethics and legal position;
- confidentiality and disclosure risk;
- storage, access and security safeguards; and
- feasibility.

Record one decision: approve, approve with conditions, refer for further review, decline, or withdrawn by the applicant. An approval must define the permitted purpose, people, data scope, storage, transfer, output review, retention and destruction conditions.

Only set **ready to issue agreement** to **Yes** when every required review and condition has been recorded.

## 3. Issue and complete the agreement

Send the applicant a private, record-specific survey invitation for the **Data Sharing Agreement**. Never send the public application link as a substitute for the agreement link.

The applicant reviews the approved scope and signs electronically. The authorised BNR signatory then countersigns the same record. Retain the applicant's certified REDCap PDF and the final executed agreement PDF in the approved private location.

Do not release data until the agreement is complete and release is authorised.

## 4. Release, monitor and close

Complete the **Release, Monitoring and Closure** instrument. Record the exact dataset ID, version and filename; who prepared and independently checked it; the disclosure check; and when, how, by whom and to whom it was transferred.

Use the approved transfer route. Record output-review decisions, any suspected incident, the end-of-access action and the evidence used to close the request.

Never place an application, non-public dataset, agreement, credential, transfer detail or review evidence in Git or in public `outputs/` folders.

::: {.callout-warning title="Stop if the approved scope changes"}
Refer the request back for review before changing its purpose, team, data scope, linkage, storage environment, transfer method or retention period.
:::
